reviews.text:
I own a cat, and I've taken him to this clinic for treatments such as when he caught a cold, lost fur, and had his neutering surgery.

I could really tell that the doctor loves animals; even my shy cat goes up to him for cuddles. (laughs)

Even though I didn't ask, he brushed my cat's teeth (which he doesn't let me do on his own) and trimmed his claws, which I was very grateful for.

He's a very kind and gentle doctor, so I feel completely at ease leaving my cat in his care.

My dog, Maru, is very well-behaved and quiet in front of this vet. Even on the same day, if you call, they can see him right away, and their explanations are thorough, so I trust them completely.

As a side note, the vet resembles Tetsuto Yamada of the Yakult Swallows.

This hospital offers antibody testing, which is still rare in Japan.
Even though there are antibodies remaining in the body, they still vaccinate dogs every year, a practice common in pet-related developed countries that eliminates the burden on your dog and the need to introduce unnecessary toxins into their body.
Is this the only hospital in Tokyo that offers lessons in behavioral therapy [JBDA skills]?
Like Sakura Animal Hospital in Aichi, they also have veterinarians on staff who are working to make hospitals "fun places, not scary places."
I would highly recommend this animal hospital, whether as your main clinic or a second one.
Dr. Motofuro is super kind!

He is a very kind doctor, easy to talk to about questions, and always examines my pet carefully. I moved and now live a little further away, but I trust him so much that he is still my regular vet. He always asks, "Is there anything else you're concerned about?" so that I don't have any worries. I can sense his high level of expertise and his dedication in explaining things in an easy-to-understand way.

This was a hospital where you could easily go even for minor issues.

It's a local doctor who readily listens to your concerns, even if the symptoms aren't urgent.

The reception staff were always kind, and the doctor was a gentle and thorough person who clearly loves animals.

I'm sad that I can no longer go there because I've moved, but I'm very grateful for all the care I received.

For those living nearby, I recommend it because it's easy to make appointments and convenient to visit.

I was a patient there until I moved.

The veterinarian was very kind and answered all my questions, and offered suggestions when necessary.

It was excellent.

The nurses are friendly and nice! But the veterinarian seems to follow the manual, and when you ask questions, they give you a fast-paced, technical explanation, giving off a strong "get home!" vibe. They do accept emergency appointments, but I suspect that's only because they had an opening.

I'd go there for everyday minor issues since it's nearby, but I wouldn't want to take my pet there for a life-threatening illness.

They have absolutely no intention of answering questions. I wouldn't recommend bringing your pet there if it's feeling unwell.
